chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi said: Abu Amr Uthman ibn Ahmad ibn Abdillah narrated to me; he said: The judge Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Razi narrated to me; he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Hasani narrated to me; he said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Farisi narrated to me; he said: Muhammad ibn Mansur narrated to me; he said: Ibrahim ibn Abdillah ibn Husayn ibn Uthman ibn Ma'alla ibn Ja'far narrated to me; he said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said:

"O Messenger of Allah, what is [the reward] for one who visits us?" He said: "Whoever visits me while alive or dead, or visits your father while alive or dead, or visits your brother while alive or dead, or visits you while alive or dead, it is a right upon me to rescue him on the Day of Resurrection."

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْت: the People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the Imams or Ahl al-Bayt according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the spiritual efficacy of Ziyarah (visitation) as a means of intercession, emphasizing that the bond transcends physical presence by covering both the living and the deceased. It underscores the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt in Shia theology, where their visitation serves as a guarantee of divine rescue (istinqaz) by the Prophet on the Day of Judgment.
